North Beach Special Use District: A new Restaurant may be approved by Conditional Use on the First Story only if the Zoning Administrator first finds the space is currently or was last legally occupied by a Restaurant or a Bar, that use was not discontinued or abandoned, and the new Restaurant will not enlarge the space. findings.text: An active ABC Type 47 license (on-sale general, eating place) has been on file at 1309 Grant Ave since March 5, 2001, issued to Ristorante Ideale.

A 1988 Conditional Use Authorization (Case No. 1987.801C) approved the exchange from Type 41 to Type 47 and expansion of the existing full-service restaurant at this address, decided January 28, 1988.

Planning Code § 780.3(c)(2)(A) in effect on June 7, 2023 requires a Conditional Use Authorization for a Restaurant to serve alcohol (Types 02, 23, 41, 47, 49, 59, or 75) on the first story in the North Beach SUD, with a Commission finding that it is and will remain a bona fide eating place with at least 51% of gross receipts from food sold on the premises.
findings.verification_note: The records reference Planning Code § 722, not § 780.3(c)(2)(A), and state the actual controls are not shown for the report date.

findings.text: The nearest comparable Type 47 upgrade (414 Columbus Ave, 51 meters away) was approved by CUA in December 2022 after nine months, with standard conditions on signage, odor control, sidewalk maintenance, community liaison, and three-year validity; no special restrictions on hours, sales mix, or occupancy were imposed.

Nine of ten dated use decisions for restaurant and bar applications within 1,000 feet in the last five years were approved (3 approved, 6 approved with conditions), one withdrawn, and zero denied, for a 90% approval rate.

The concept profile states the business currently holds a Type 41, but ABC records show an active Type 47 at this address as of June 7, 2023; the records do not establish whether two licenses exist, one has lapsed, or the profile is outdated.

basis.text: The licence looked up is ABC Type 47 (on-sale general, eating place), as stated in the description.

A Type 47 licence is an on-sale general licence. State law limits these to one for each 2,000 inhabitants of the county; in a county over that number ABC issues no additional one, so the licence comes by transfer of an existing licence unless state law allows otherwise.
Census tract 106.00: 59 active on-sale retail licences in ABC's licences as they stood on 7 June 2023, against 12 authorised in ABC's census tract authorisations of September 2026.

The tract is over its authorised number. State law tests a new licence and a transfer from other premises for undue concentration, and the applicant does not say how the liquor licence will be obtained.

The description does not give how the liquor licence will be obtained (new, or a transfer from another owner or another location), so the rules cannot say which licence rules apply: insufficient information.

Licences with an unknown status on 2023-06-07: 15 ABC licences within 1,000 ft and 13 in the census tract were on file, but ABC's daily reports do not show their status that day (it changed two or more times since). They are left out of the licence counts, the census tract count and what the space is read as.

findings.text: Type 47 is a quota license; new licenses are issued only through ABC's annual priority drawing if the county has headroom, otherwise the license must be purchased on the open market and transferred (person-to-person and premises-to-premises transfer), a process that takes 90–180 days including escrow, posting, and local zoning sign-off, with license prices running $100,000–$450,000 in San Francisco.
findings.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

findings.text: If the existing Type 47 license (ABC #372058) is still active and held by the current operator, the project may be framed as a continuation of that license rather than a new transfer, avoiding the undue concentration test and quota purchase; the records do not show the current licensee name or whether the license has been transferred since 2001.
ABC sends all license applications (original or transfer) to the Police Department ABC Liaison Unit and to the Planning Department for review under Business and Professions Code § 23987.
findings.verification_note: The cited catalog entry describes the license type, fees, and transfer process but does not mention interagency referrals or § 23987.

filing_playbook.action: Confirm the status of the existing Type 47 license (ABC #372058) and the 1988 CUA conditions with San Francisco Planning and ABC.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Contact the Planning Department Zoning Counter or Planner on Duty and ask: (1) Is ABC license #372058, a Type 47 issued in 2001 to Ristorante Ideale at 1309 Grant Ave, still active under the current operator, or has it lapsed? (2) Does the 1988 Conditional Use Authorization (Case No. 1987.801C) remain in effect, and if so, request a copy of the motion with all conditions of approval. (3) Does the Department consider a change of operator or a license upgrade under an active Type 47 at this address to be a continuation of the existing use, or does it require a new CUA? Contact ABC Northern Division in Oakland or check the online license query to confirm the license status and current licensee name. Frame the inquiry as preliminary due diligence before filing, and confirm in writing to avoid conflicting guidance later.

filing_playbook.action: Register the business with the SF Treasurer for a Business Registration Certificate, and file a Fictitious Business Name statement if the DBA differs from the legal entity name.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Register with the SF Office of the Treasurer & Tax Collector within 30 days of starting business; the fee is tiered by gross receipts (e.g., $55 up to $100k, $95 up to $250k, each plus a $4 state fee) and the registration year runs April 1 to March 31. You will receive a Business Account Number (BAN) needed for all other city permits. If the public-facing name (e.g., Ristorante Ideale) differs from the legal entity name, file a Fictitious Business Name statement with the County Clerk in person or by mail with photo ID, then publish in a court-approved newspaper once a week for four weeks and file proof of publication within 45 days (total cost $60–$120).
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

filing_playbook.action: Obtain a California Seller's Permit (sales tax) and an Employer Identification Number (EIN) if not already held.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Apply online with the California Department of Tax and Fee Administration (CDTFA) for a seller's permit; there is no fee and it is often issued the same day. ABC requires the seller's permit before issuing a liquor license. If the business does not yet have a federal EIN, apply online with the IRS (free, issued immediately Mon–Fri); the EIN is needed to open a business bank account, register for payroll taxes, and apply for the ABC license. Also register with the California Employment Development Department (EDD) for payroll taxes within 15 days of paying more than $100 in wages in a quarter (free, online, takes 1–7 days); your payroll provider needs the EDD account number.

filing_playbook.action: Ensure all employees obtain California Food Handler Cards and that at least one manager holds a Certified Food Protection Manager certificate.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Every employee who handles food must obtain a California Food Handler Card within 30 days of hire from an ANSI-accredited online course (about $7–$15, valid 3 years); the online course takes about two hours. At least one owner or employee must pass an accredited food safety certification exam (ServSafe, Prometric, NRFSP, or 360training) and hold a Certified Food Protection Manager certificate within 60 days of opening; DPH asks for this certificate at the pre-opening inspection (course plus exam about $100–$250, valid 5 years). All alcohol servers and their managers must complete Responsible Beverage Service (RBS) certification within 60 days of hire: register on the ABC RBS Portal ($3), complete an approved course (about $10–$25), and pass the exam; keep the certification list on site for ABC inspections.

filing_playbook.action: Obtain workers' compensation insurance, ASCAP and BMI music licenses, and subscribe to organics recycling service before opening.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Workers' compensation insurance is mandatory from the first employee (even part-time); quote through a broker or the State Compensation Insurance Fund and provide proof of coverage to DPH and the Entertainment Commission if needed. Subscribe to ASCAP and BMI public performance licenses ($300–$2,500 each per year, formula-based on occupancy and music use) to cover background music and any live or recorded music played publicly; sign up online and the licenses are effective immediately. Set up organics (green bin) collection service with your hauler before opening (required under SB 1383 for all food businesses); the city enforces it through the business license or health inspection.

timeline_cost.notes: The time and cost ranges are for the approvals in the entitlement path when they are granted: Conditional Use Authorization (if required), Health Permit to Operate, and Building Permit (if building work is proposed). The CUA timeline is 120–300 days from filing to approval (based on the catalog entry for sf.conditional_use_authorization, which is not in this catalog but is consistent with the 9-month approval at 414 Columbus Ave, app:datasf_planning:2022-002108CUA); the Health Permit is 14–45 days (catalog:sf.health_permit); the Building Permit for work without a change of use is 14–120 days (catalog:sf.building_permit, though not formally in the path because no tenant improvements are stated). The government cost includes the ABC Type 47 license transfer or purchase ($17,000–$450,000, catalog:ca.abc_type_47), the CUA application fee (approximately $3,100, not in the catalog but stated in the sf.conditional_use_authorization notes), the Health Permit application ($470, catalog:sf.health_permit), and city/state registration fees (business registration $55–$700, seller's permit $0, EDD $0, entity registration $70–$150, catalog entries). The ranges assume the Type 47 is acquired by transfer; if the existing license (ABC #372058) is still active and continues, the cost drops to the lower end (no license purchase, only the transfer filing fee of roughly $1,000–$1,600). If Planning determines that no new CUA is required because the 1988 authorization remains in effect and the project is a continuation, the timeline drops to 90–120 days (ABC transfer plus health permit) and the cost to $17,000–$18,000. These figures are times and costs to approval; they do not cover a denial or a withdrawal. The ABC license transfer timeline (90–240 days) includes escrow, posting, ABC investigation, and local agency referrals but assumes no protest or Public Convenience or Necessity (PCN) hearing; a protest or PCN finding would add 1–3 months. No tenant improvements are stated, so no building permit time or cost is included unless construction is proposed. Confirm the pathway with Planning before incurring costs.

records_summary: 1309 Grant Ave sits in the North Beach Neighborhood Commercial District with significant overlay restrictions on restaurant and bar alcohol service. The space is an existing restaurant (Ristorante Ideale) that has held an active Type 47 license since 2001, originally authorized in 1988 for the upgrade from Type 41 to Type 47. The records show a conditional-use posture for intensifying an existing restaurant's alcohol service in North Beach: Planning Code § 780.3(c)(2)(A) requires a CUA with a finding that the restaurant is and will remain a bona fide eating place serving at least 51% of gross receipts from food. The block is extraordinarily dense—57 food/drink businesses and 45 on-sale licenses within 500 ft—but the last five years show a 90% approval rate (N=10 dated use decisions) for comparable restaurant and bar applications nearby, nearly all continuations of existing uses or license transfers with no space expansion.
data_gaps: The records do not show whether the existing Type 47 license (ABC #372058, issued 2001) is still active under the current operator or was transferred/surrendered; ABC status says ACTIVE as of 2023-06-07 but does not name the current licensee.
No conditions of approval are extracted for the 1988 CUA (Case No. 1987.801C) that authorized the Type 41→47 upgrade; those conditions may still bind the premises.

The concept profile states the business currently holds a Type 41, but the ABC records show an active Type 47 at this address; clarify whether two licenses are on file or whether the profile is outdated.

Hearing transcripts, staff reports, and neighbor comment summaries are not available for the key CUA cases, so the basis for approval (the bona fide eating place finding, any kitchen or seating minimums, any hours restrictions) is not shown.

No SFPUC FOG wastewater permit or DBI building permit history is in the bundle; if the kitchen or seating layout changed after 1988 those records would show whether the space complies with current DPH and fire code for the stated use.
